recommendation: Keep this audit commit as-is. Reverting subscriberId to a scalar string or 0..1 would conflict with later Published decisions; any future concern should be filed as a new wording/modeling tracker rather than treated as incomplete FHIR-12241 application.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive Financial Management issue asking that Coverage.subscriberId remain separate from Coverage.identifier because folding the subscriber/member/card number into a general identifier list makes the value ambiguous when multiple identifiers are present.
initial_application: No commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-12241 was found. Commit 43806174288e821cb06173a72cde96317186412b reintroduced Coverage.subscriberId as a separate 0..1 string in the Coverage spreadsheet source and removed Subscriber Id from Coverage.identifier wording, matching the seed request despite the missing issue key.
additional_context: Later Published Coverage issues FHIR-24638 and FHIR-24688 intentionally changed the restored element to Identifier and then to 0..*. Both are already represented on the combined branch, including source-fixing AutoFHIR commits for stale model-definition metadata. Coverage is active in source/fhir.ini, and community searches found no direct FHIR-12241 discussion or conflicting decision.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current Coverage StructureDefinition keeps Coverage.identifier and Coverage.subscriberId separate, defines subscriberId as Identifier [0..*], includes a subscriberid search parameter, includes examples with subscriberId, and exposes subscriberId as repeating FHIR.Identifier in the FHIR model-definition Library.

related_jiras.note: Published/Persuasive R5 issue that intentionally changed Coverage.subscriberId from string to Identifier after the separate element was restored.
